question: Obtain the expression for the radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom and state how it depends on $n$.

options.A: Combining the force condition with Bohr quantisation gives $r_n=\dfrac{\pi me^2}{\varepsilon_0h^2}n^2$, so radius decreases as $n^2$.
options.B: Using $\dfrac{mv^2}{r}=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{r^2}$ and $mvr=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ gives $r_n=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0h^2}{\pi me^2}n^2$. Therefore, $r_n\propto n^2$.
options.C: $r_n=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0h^2}{\pi me^2n^2}$, so radius decreases as $n$ increases.
options.D: $r_n=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi m}$, so radius is directly proportional to $n$.
